Add PHP language support to aptu-coder using the official `tree-sitter-php` grammar. After this change, `analyze_directory`, `analyze_file` and `analyze_module` extract functions, methods, classes, interfaces, traits, enums, calls, imports and inheritance from `.php` files instead of returning the unsupported-extension fallback.

## Context

- PHP is one of the most widely deployed server-side languages and is absent from the registry: no `php` in `EXTENSION_MAP` (`crates/aptu-coder-core/src/lang.rs`), no handler in `crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/`, no `tree-sitter-php` in `Cargo.lock`.
- aptu-coder already supports mainstream languages such as Java, Kotlin, Swift and TypeScript. PHP should follow the same registry pattern as the existing object-oriented languages.

## Prerequisites

None.

## Where to Look

- **Handler templates:** `crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/java.rs` (an OO language with `extends` / `implements`) and `swift.rs` (inheritance through named children, inline tests).
- **Grammar:** the `tree-sitter-php` repository on GitHub. Node kinds and field names come from `php/src/node-types.json`; the crate entry points are on docs.rs.
- **Registry:** `languages/mod.rs` (handler registration) and `lang.rs` (extension map and supported-language list).

## Scope

- A new handler, `crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/php.rs`, with the SPDX header and the five query constants used by the other handlers (`ELEMENT_QUERY`, `CALL_QUERY`, `REFERENCE_QUERY`, `IMPORT_QUERY`, `DEFUSE_QUERY`).
- An `extract_inheritance` handler with the same contract as the Java handler.
- Registry wiring for `"php"` in both `languages/mod.rs` and `lang.rs`.
- Unit tests in `php.rs` and one integration test file under `crates/aptu-coder/tests/`.
- `README.md`: add PHP to the Supported Languages list and the intro count.

You choose the crate version, the node kinds and fields, the query text, the grammar entry point and the handler slots to wire. The crate must clear `cargo deny`'s package age check without `SKIP_PACKAGE_AGE_CHECK`.

## Suggested Approach

1. Pick the crate version from crates.io and check it against the workspace `tree-sitter` version.
2. Parse a small sample `.php` file with the grammar and list the node kinds and fields you see. Confirm each one in `php/src/node-types.json` before you use it.
3. Write the five queries and prove they compile in a unit test before wiring anything. The tree-sitter query syntax documentation covers captures and fields.
4. Mirror the registry wiring of the most recent language addition.
5. Add the unit tests and the integration test last.

Expect a day or two of work; most of it is step 2.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tree-sitter-php` is declared in the root `[workspace.dependencies]` and in `crates/aptu-coder-core/Cargo.toml`; `Cargo.lock` is updated; `cargo deny check advisories licenses bans` passes without `SKIP_PACKAGE_AGE_CHECK`
- [ ] `crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/php.rs` exists with the SPDX header, the five query constants and `extract_inheritance`
- [ ] `php` is in `EXTENSION_MAP` and in `supported_languages()` in `lang.rs`
- [ ] `"php"` is wired into `get_language_info()` and `get_ts_language()` in `languages/mod.rs`
- [ ] `analyze_file` on a `.php` file returns `language: "php"` and lists functions, methods, class / interface / trait / enum declarations, free, `->` and `::` calls, and `use` imports
- [ ] `analyze_module` on the same file returns the same element set; `analyze_directory` labels it `php`
- [ ] `extract_inheritance` on `class Foo extends Bar implements A, B` returns `["extends Bar", "implements A", "implements B"]`; on a class with no clauses it returns `[]`
- [ ] A `.php` file that mixes HTML and `<?php ... ?>` parses with zero ERROR nodes and yields the same PHP elements as the PHP-only equivalent
- [ ] Unit tests in `php.rs` cover: the queries compile, the element query matches a class and a function, the inheritance happy path and the no-clause edge case
- [ ] An integration test covers one happy path and the HTML-template edge case, using `common::call_tool_raw` and `tempfile::NamedTempFile` as in `tests/integration_tests.rs`
- [ ] `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --locked --profile ci -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass
- [ ] REUSE compliance passes; the binary size delta is stated in the PR description
- [ ] Commits are GPG signed and DCO signed off

## Not in Scope

- `extract_function_name`, `find_method_for_receiver`, `find_receiver_type` (no consumer since #1807)
- Trait `use` resolution, property and constant extraction, attributes, namespace import aliasing
- `.phtml`, `.inc`, `.module`, `.php5` extensions
- Tool handler or schema changes; other languages

## Note on Process

The maintainers are implementing this in-house. External pull requests for this issue are not being accepted at this time and will be closed.

## Related

- #648 and #1742: the Swift integration, the most recent language addition
- #1063: binary size delta reporting

aptu-coder

A Model Context Protocol (MCP) code-intelligence server that gives AI coding agents pre-parsed symbol tables instead of raw file bytes, cutting token usage by up to 59% in the cited benchmark conditions (see Benchmarks). OpenSSF silver certified: fewer than 1% of open source projects reach this level.

> [!NOTE] > Native agent tools (regex search, path matching, file reading) handle targeted lookups well. `aptu-coder` handles the mechanical, non-AI work: mapping directory structure and extracting symbols, so a coding agent's context window is spent reasoning instead of re-deriving structure on every call. Most code-intelligence tooling for AI agents indexes a codebase into a cloud embedding or vector store and retrieves by similarity search. aptu-coder instead parses the codebase on-device with tree-sitter and serves it locally over MCP: no source code leaves the machine, and retrieval is exact (symbol tables) rather than approximate (nearest-neighbor similarity). ## Benchmarks Paired comprehension tasks on Claude Code (MCP mode vs native shell search). Methodology: [Django](https://github.com/django/django) auth migration ([v12](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/aptu-coder/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/v12/methodology.md)) and [OpenFAST](https://github.com/OpenFAST/openfast) AeroDyn integration audit ([v13](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/aptu-coder/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/v13/methodology.md)). | Task | Mode | Sonnet 4.6 | Haiku 4.5 | Savings | |---|---|---|---|---| | Django (Python) | MCP | 112k tokens, $0.39 | 406k tokens, $0.42 | **59% fewer tokens, 59% cheaper** (Sonnet) | | Django (Python) | Native | 276k tokens, $0.95 | 473k tokens, $0.53 | 14% fewer tokens, 21% cheaper (Haiku) | | OpenFAST (Fortran) | MCP | 472k tokens, $1.65 | 687k tokens, $0.72 | **46% fewer tokens, 42% cheaper** (Sonnet) | | OpenFAST (Fortran) | Native | 877k tokens, $2.85 | 2162k tokens, $2.21 | **68% fewer tokens, 68% cheaper** (Haiku) | A real end-to-end multi-agent run against this repository itself: five refactoring issues (#1578–#1582) fixed by the [coder skill](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/agentic-coder-skill) in one orchestrated session — 23 subagent spawns (5 scout, 1 guard, 10 build, 7 check), ~1h42m, three human interventions — producing PRs #1584–#1588, all merged with CI green. [Case study](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/agentic-coder-skill/blob/main/docs/examples/2026-09-aptu-coder-5-issues.md). ### Scope of the benchmark claims The token-savings figures above come from single, focused comprehension tasks where the agent used aptu-coder instead of shell search. Agentic coding loops have bash and ripgrep and can search the repo directly. The [v19 benchmark program](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/aptu-coder/blob/main/docs/audit/2026-09-30-v19-pivot.md) (N=20 paired sessions, pre-registered claim gate) measured aptu-coder in those loops: no measurable answer-quality gain over bash + ripgrep on structural fan-in tasks (pooled paired F1 diff mean -0.071, 95% CI [-0.179, +0.038]; gate NOT-SUPPORTED); tool activation itself was reliable when tools were surfaced directly. Recommended uses: premise grounding for multi-agent workflows, and non-agentic MCP consumers (IDE assistants, CI jobs, scoring pipelines). ## Overview

*Figure 1: An AI agent connects over MCP to aptu-coder, whose analyze tools feed tree-sitter parsing into the formatter.* aptu-coder is a comprehension layer for coding agents: it gives an agent harness precise structural context about a codebase, directory trees, and symbol definitions, without the agent reading raw files or re-deriving structure on every call. That prevents context starvation on large or unfamiliar codebases while keeping the result set small enough to fit the model's context window. It supports 18 languages (see [Supported Languages](#supported-languages)) and integrates with any MCP-compatible orchestrator. Structural context is built once and reused: an on-disk cache keyed by blake3 content hashes keeps results correct across concurrent writes. For consumers that hold source text without an on-disk path, `aptu-coder-core` also exposes `analyze_str` as a public Rust library API (see [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/aptu-coder/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)). Further reading on the design philosophy, from the author's [blog](https://clouatre.ca/blog/): [The Agentic SDLC Governance Stack](https://clouatre.ca/blog/ai-sdlc-governance-stack/), [Context Engineering for Multi-Agent Reliability](https://clouatre.ca/blog/context-engineering-multi-agent-reliability/), and [Orchestrating AI Agents: Subagent Architecture](https://clouatre.ca/blog/orchestrating-ai-agents-subagent-architecture/). ## Supported Languages Astro, C/C++, C#, CSS, Fortran, Go, HTML, Java, JavaScript, JSON, Kotlin, Markdown, Python, Rust, TOML, TSX, TypeScript, YAML. The full extension map lives in [`crates/aptu-coder-core/src/lang.rs`](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/aptu-coder/blob/main/crates/aptu-coder-core/src/lang.rs). ## Installation ### Homebrew (macOS and Linux) ```bash brew install clouatre-labs/tap/aptu-coder ``` Update: `brew upgrade aptu-coder` ### cargo-binstall (no Rust required) ```bash cargo binstall aptu-coder ``` ### cargo install (requires Rust toolchain) ```bash cargo install aptu-coder ``` ## Quick Start ### Build from source ```bash cargo build --release ``` The binary is at `target/release/aptu-coder`. ### Configure MCP Client **stdio (default)** — the client spawns and owns the server process; this works with orchestrators that spawn delegates (goose, pi) as well as single clients: ```bash claude mcp add --transport stdio aptu-coder -- aptu-coder ``` Or add manually to `.mcp.json` at your project root (shared with your team via version control): ```json { "mcpServers": { "aptu-coder": { "command": "aptu-coder", "args": [] } } } ``` **Streamable HTTP (optional)** — runs a single shared server process instead of one per client. A Model Context Protocol (MCP) code-intelligence server that gives AI coding agents pre-parsed symbol tables instead of raw file bytes, cutting token usage by up to 59% in the cited benchmark conditions (see Benchmarks). OpenSSF silver certified: fewer than 1% of open source projects reach this level.

> [!NOTE] > Native agent tools (regex search, path matching, file reading) handle targeted lookups well. `aptu-coder` handles the mechanical, non-AI work: mapping directory structure and extracting symbols, so a coding agent's context window is spent reasoning instead of re-deriving structure on every call. Most code-intelligence tooling for AI agents indexes a codebase into a cloud embedding or vector store and retrieves by similarity search. aptu-coder instead parses the codebase on-device with tree-sitter and serves it locally over MCP: no source code leaves the machine, and retrieval is exact (symbol tables) rather than approximate (nearest-neighbor similarity). ## Benchmarks Paired comprehension tasks on Claude Code (MCP mode vs native shell search). Methodology: [Django](https://github.com/django/django) auth migration ([v12](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/aptu-coder/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/v12/methodology.md)) and [OpenFAST](https://github.com/OpenFAST/openfast) AeroDyn integration audit ([v13](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/aptu-coder/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/v13/methodology.md)). | Task | Mode | Sonnet 4.6 | Haiku 4.5 | Savings | |---|---|---|---|---| | Django (Python) | MCP | 112k tokens, $0.39 | 406k tokens, $0.42 | **59% fewer tokens, 59% cheaper** (Sonnet) | | Django (Python) | Native | 276k tokens, $0.95 | 473k tokens, $0.53 | 14% fewer tokens, 21% cheaper (Haiku) | | OpenFAST (Fortran) | MCP | 472k tokens, $1.65 | 687k tokens, $0.72 | **46% fewer tokens, 42% cheaper** (Sonnet) | | OpenFAST (Fortran) | Native | 877k tokens, $2.85 | 2162k tokens, $2.21 | **68% fewer tokens, 68% cheaper** (Haiku) | A real end-to-end multi-agent run against this repository itself: five refactoring issues (#1578–#1582) fixed by the [coder skill](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/agentic-coder-skill) in one orchestrated session — 23 subagent spawns (5 scout, 1 guard, 10 build, 7 check), ~1h42m, three human interventions — producing PRs #1584–#1588, all merged with CI green. [Case study](https://github.com/clouatre-labs/agentic-coder-skill/blob/main/docs/examples/2026-09-aptu-coder-5-issues.md). ### Scope of the benchmark claims The token-savings figures above come from single, focused comprehension tasks where the agent used aptu-coder instead of shell search. That prevents context starvation on large or unfamiliar codebases while keeping the result set small enough to fit the model's context window. It supports 18 languages (see [Supported Languages](#supported-languages)) and integrates with any MCP-compatible orchestrator. Structural context is built once and reused: an on-disk cache keyed by blake3 content hashes keeps results correct across concurrent writes.
